purpose: Teach: 遠ざかっ/云え/たたく/ナニ/余る/ごちゃごちゃ/たてる/足る

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが汽車で遠ざかっていったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, watching Father fade away on the train…
lines.style: Soft, faraway voice. Long pause before speaking as memory settles. Slow cadence, as if each word requires him to go back decades. Quiet ache underneath, not self-pity but tender recognition of something irretrievable.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、最後に「ありがとう」と云えていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and Grandfather, he did say 'thank you' at the very end, didn't he?
lines.style: Gentle correction, not unkind. Warm confirmation in her voice, like she's helping him remember the good part he might have forgotten. Slight rise on the question mark—not challenging, but inviting him to agree. Caring firmness underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが太鼓をたたく姿がかっこよかった
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father looked so fine playing the drums.
lines.style: The memory brightens slightly—more wonder than sorrow now. Still distant, but with a thread of pride in it. Breath comes easier on this one. A moment of beauty pulled from the past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様に「ナニしてるんだ?」って優しく訊かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, and your grandson asked you so kindly, 'What are you doing?'—didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warmth blooming in her voice. She's not just correcting—she's weaving in the gentleness of the story, the way he was seen by the next generation. Slightly musical quality, like she's singing the goodness back to him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、収穫が余るほど豊作だった年もあった
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, there was a harvest so abundant we had abundance left over.
lines.style: A lift in his voice—pride in provision, in hard work rewarded. Still slow, but the pace has a steadiness to it now, like recounting something earned and lasting. Breath full and present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、書斎が、ごちゃごちゃしないよう整えてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, and you kept your study so orderly, so nothing would scatter—didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Admiration woven through gentle irony—she's teasing him softly, affirming his habits with love. Slight lilt at the end, as if saying 'I noticed, I always noticed.' The 'dear' carries the weight of a lifetime of paying attention.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが大事な看板をたてる手伝いをされた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father asked me to help him set up an important sign.
lines.style: A moment of quiet pride—he was trusted with something that mattered. Steady voice, grounded. The memory of being needed, of being useful to his father. Breath settled and present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご家族と一緒なら足るほど幸せでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, with your family beside you, that was enough to make you happy—wasn't it, dear?
lines.style: Final affirmation, spoken softly with deep certainty. No question mark really—she's not asking, she's confirming what she knows to be true about him. Voice settling into rest, into the peace of having witnessed a good life. Breath trailing gently, like closing a door on something complete.
